testCase.name: [local] S23 Browser clock a day off: a task closed by Save & Extract is stamped with server time and stays in Finished Tasks

descriptionHtml:
Bug B18 · P1 · known

Many dates and times follow the device clock instead of server time (UAT 3.8): 'NEW TODAY', admit date, vitals date, task done time, transcript date; with a phone two days slow a held drug is stamped two days back and the next cleanup deletes it

Tickets: TFA-92584 ready for qa (UAT 3.8); TFA-92597 ready for qa (R6); TFA-92579 AC 3/4 ready for qa (NEW TODAY); TFA-94745 ready for qa (draft restore) · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: local

Note: Root cause known (Daniela asked for server time on 10-03); the deleted drug, missing badge and wrong draft restore are new symptoms. TC-16/S18 (UAT 3.8, one device set to the wrong date): a phone a day ahead files its bedside line in a row dated tomorrow on the shared record, and the next write from a correctly clocked device lists the lines before it twice (the transcript archive trusts the device date). Which calendar day a correct device should use when its local day and the server's UTC day differ is the open question Q9 (D10); TC-16/S25 passed otherwise. Review 2026-10-14 (TFA-92579/92584): a browser whose day is ahead writes the badge roll back to the server, and every device shows Follow-up, with the matching template and billing family (TC-01/S08, TC-20/S20a; TFA-92584 AC 8). The failing cell of TC-25/S24a is the card's NEW TODAY, which compares addedAt with the device's date (PatientCard.tsx:154-156). EFS/S28 (a)(b) restore drafts by the device date (TFA-94745); (c), an old draft put in today's box, is B13's. Review 2026-10-15 (TFA-94514): the analytics day is the device date too (pilotUsageEvents / pilotDailyRounding use localDay()): a phone 3 days ahead files its rows under its own day, and an encounter across the phone midnight is split over two days and never timed (OAT-06/S10).

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): TC-01/S08, TC-10/S22, TC-12/S23, TC-19/S19, TC-25/S24a, TC-02/S13b, EFS/S28, TC-16/S18, TC-06/S19, OAT-06/S10, TC-06/S23, TC-21/S22, TC-25/S24b, TC-19/S23

Approach · TC-22 Task Closure & Extraction · S23 Browser clock a day off: a task closed by Save & Extract is stamped with server time and stays in Finished Tasks

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U13 Task retention and clock: Hospital completed tasks clear at 16 h; Hospital open tasks clear 36 h after the chart was last processed; … (UAT 3.6; UAT 3.8)
  • U8 All of the above in Nursing Home as well as Hospital, passing in both (UAT TC-22 step 4; UAT 3.3; TFA-92592 AC 14) — gate: blocked: TFA-92592 ready for pr

Test design technique: Error guessing (error-guessing) — Go straight for the places most likely to break (failures, double clicks, two tabs, a wrong clock, injected instructions).

Given Fresh @roundai.test account on the local stack; a Hospital patient and a Nursing Home resident with 'follow up BMP' and 'recheck weight in two weeks'; Playwright context with page.clock.setSystemTime(server now + 24 h), and a second run with server now − 24 h; …

When Tap Save & Extract; read the task's doneAt through a read-only backend query (rounding:list / snf:list); reload the list so applyLifecycle runs; open Task Export and expand Finished Tasks

Then doneAt within ±5 min of server time in both runs; after the lifecycle run 'follow up BMP' is still under Finished Tasks

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): UAT 3.8: every time-based rule uses the server clock. Predicted Fail on main: useEncounterTasks.ts and useSaveAndExtract.ts stamp doneAt with new Date(), so the −24 h run is cleared at once by the server-time 16 h rule and the +24 h run would keep it about 40 h. The Task Export row shows no closed time, so the stored value decides. The same rule on the tap path is TC-07 S28; …

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (blocked)

S23 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-22.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row.

Issue type: New product issue · environment local · tickets TFA-92592 ready for qa; TFA-92585 ready for pr

On a phone whose clock is a day behind, a task closed by Save & Extract is stamped with the phone's time and disappears from Finished Tasks as soon as the list reloads; a day ahead, it lingers about 40 h instead of 16 h.

Evidence: allure-results/2ecd961c…: all 4 runs put doneAt at device time ±1440 min. With the Hospital clock 24 h behind, the closed task drops out of Finished Tasks after the list reloads. The NH half is already recorded (docs/2026-10-13-pr106-review.md S3) and fixed on PR #106 head 35edc8b (clockNow), not merged. The Hospital stamp (useEncounterTasks.ts new Date()) is unchanged on #106 and appears nowhere else (dev report, ledger, knownGaps); a matrix risk predicted it.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 43c38a4f (10-15 re-tests), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: PW · Playwright script; secondary: CODEREVIEW · Code review — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: newspec-c.

UAT item: TC-22 Task Closure & Extraction · Section: A5 · Cross-Cutting · Scenario: TC-22/S23

Browser clock a day off: a task closed by Save & Extract is stamped with server time and stays in Finished Tasks

Tickets: TFA-92592 In-Room Dictation & Note Generation (ready for qa)

New local lane newspec-c: status failed in newspec-c/results.json → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue; part of it is a known gap)).

How it is tested (newspec-c/plan.json, automatable: yes): New Playwright spec, two runs (browser clock server now + 24 h and - 24 h), each in both contexts: fresh account, Hospital patient and Nursing Home resident with 'follow up BMP' and 'recheck weight in two weeks'; ai/parsing:extractTasks answered at the socket to close 'follow up BMP'. Save & Extract; read the task's doneAt (rounding:list / snf:list) against time:now (+-5 min); reload the list so applyLifecycle runs; open Task Export, expand Finished Tasks and look for 'follow up BMP'. Nursing Home: 'still under Finished Tasks' is recorded only (TC-22 Q12, no retention stated for completed Nursing Home tasks); doneAt is judged in both contexts. — Clock, socket answer and the account's own reads are all scriptable.

Detail:

Local stack on main 43c38a4f; every model call the page makes is answered in the page by ext-support.ts (an ai/* call it is not told about is failed, never forwarded) and the tripwire showed no model call. Spec ext-tc22-s23-clock.spec.ts (copy of tc22-clock.spec.ts with its own evidence), 4 runs. Clock +24 h: doneAt = device time, +1440 min from server time, both contexts. Clock −24 h: doneAt −1440 min, both contexts; after the list reload the Hospital task is removed and not under Finished Tasks (U13: completed tasks stay 16 h). Nursing Home −24 h is removed too (recorded only, Q12). Same as on e02167f; useEncounterTasks.ts / useSaveAndExtract.ts still stamp new Date(). Known: B18 (device clock instead of server time, UAT 3.8).

Product issue: On a device whose clock is a day behind, a task closed by Save & Extract disappears from Task Export > Finished Tasks at the next list load; a day ahead, it would stay ~40 h instead of 16 h (doneAt follows the device clock, UAT 3.8).

Known gap (known): true

Evidence: 8 attached.

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Lane A (our scripted spec, not written yet): page.clock in the browser and ai/parsing:extractTasks mocked with trackActionRequests on a fresh local account, so the stamp, not the model, is under test; dev has no admin key, one shared account and no action mock, so it runs on the local stack only …. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
